question: Should OpenClaw add a broader config mode that disables tokenized Gateway/Control UI auth, HTTPS or Tailscale URL constraints, device identity, pairing, and related HTTP/Control UI auth checks for private deployments?
rationale: The requested behavior changes Gateway operator-auth and transport security boundaries and adds public config surface, so automation cannot choose the permanent policy safely.

options.title: Keep Current Boundaries
options.body: Treat token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale identity, and existing break-glass paths as the supported surface and reject a blanket urlToken bypass.

options.title: Sponsor Narrow Dangerous Mode
options.body: Design a named private-ingress or tailnet policy with explicit warnings, audit checks, docs, startup checks, and tests instead of a generic toggle.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Auth Items
options.body: Resolve the smaller auth-mode, layered-auth, and Control UI HTTP-read questions in their own issues before deciding whether a broader bypass should exist.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Boundaries
recommendation.body: Treat token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale identity, and existing break-glass paths as the supported surface and reject a blanket urlToken bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history across Tailscale auth scoping, Gateway auth hardening, and the adjacent no-auth exposure fix.
